candidate.title: snRNA-Seq
candidate.scope: The middle snRNA-Seq row of the supplied Illumina poster crop, associated by the listed Grindberg et al. (2013) reference with RNA-sequencing from single nuclei. It depicts a single-nucleus, poly(A)-RNA-to-cDNA library architecture ending in indexed P5/P7 fragments. Smart-Seq2 and FRISCR are independently labelled neighboring rows, with no connecting arrows to snRNA-Seq; their operations and the adjacent LNA chemical legend are context, not alternative targets of this card. This is the drawn implementation, not a claim that every snRNA-seq protocol uses the same preparation or chemistry.

Abstract, opening description of cDNA sequencing
evidence.quote: It has recently been established that synthesis of double-stranded cDNA can be done from a single cell for use in DNA sequencing.

operations.label: Lyse and centrifuge
operations.description: Disrupt the cells in suspension and centrifuge the resulting material, separating a nuclei fraction from supernatant. The nuclei fraction continues to sorting.
operations.mechanism: Cell lysis and centrifugal fractionation are specified by the caption; the tube distinguishes the resulting compartments.
operations.information_effect: The retained material changes from whole cells to nuclei, restricting the represented RNA source to the nuclear preparation; this does not establish perfectly pure nuclear RNA.

evidence.locator: snRNA-Seq row: cell suspension arrow to Lyse and centrifuge; tube labelled Supernatant and Nuclei
snRNA-Seq row, nuclei fraction retained after Lyse and centrifuge
evidence.rationale: Retaining nuclei rather than whole cells changes the represented biological compartment. Fractionation alone does not establish absence of carryover.

operations.label: Sort nuclei
operations.description: Select an individual nucleus from the nuclei fraction for the subsequent cDNA workflow.
operations.information_effect: Retains association with a single biological nucleus before RNA information is copied into DNA; no mixing of nuclear contents is shown.

evidence.locator: snRNA-Seq row: tube, Sort nuclei arrow, Nucleus boundary and arrow toward First strand synthesis

operations.label: First strand synthesis
operations.description: Copy the nucleus-derived poly(A) RNA into a complementary first DNA strand. The resulting intermediate displays an adapter-associated T tract paired to the RNA A tract and a CCC end. The diagram compresses access to the nuclear RNA into this interface and shows no separate nuclear-lysis or RNA-purification operation.
operations.mechanism: The drawn A/T pairing supports oligo-dT-associated priming and reverse transcription; this row does not name the reverse transcriptase or define the CCC-generating reaction.
operations.information_effect: Transfers transcript-sequence information from RNA to cDNA. The poly(A)/oligo-dT interface supports a polyadenylated-RNA representation, not a claim of unbiased recovery of all nuclear RNA.

evidence.rationale: Complementary A/T tracts plus an adapter-bearing first-strand product support interpreting this as oligo-dT-associated copying of poly(A) RNA; enzyme identity is withheld.

operations.label: cDNA synthesis
operations.description: Extend or complete the cDNA intermediate into the depicted end-handle arrangement with the left GGG/CCC junction and right adapter-associated end. The caption does not separately identify second-strand synthesis.
operations.mechanism: The drawn change is formation of the paired GGG/CCC handle and cDNA extension; exact enzymes, template-switch oligo composition and timing of second-strand completion are not specified in this row.
operations.information_effect: Produces a DNA substrate that retains transcript-derived sequence between the depicted end handles and can be amplified.

operations.label: PCR
operations.description: Amplify the end-tagged cDNA, producing the double-stranded DNA substrate for tagmentation.
operations.mechanism: PCR is explicitly labelled between cDNA synthesis and Tagmentation.
operations.information_effect: Increases copies of represented transcript-derived cDNA. Copy number after amplification is not an original-molecule count.

evidence.rationale: PCR denotes DNA-copy amplification. operations.label: Tagmentation
operations.description: Transform amplified cDNA into fragments bearing the depicted adapter-associated segments for final library completion.
operations.mechanism: Tagmentation couples DNA fragmentation with adapter tagging; the blue enzyme icons are catalytic components of this operation, not a separate analyte branch.
operations.information_effect: Carries nuclear transcript-derived insert sequence into a DNA-fragment library; no end-specific transcript readout or strand-preservation scheme is specified.

evidence.rationale: Interpreting the labelled tagmentation operation as fragmentation coupled to adapter tagging explains the change from amplified cDNA to fragments that receive final P5/P7/index ends. No enzyme identity or cut-site specificity is inferred.

operations.label: Gap repair and PCR
operations.description: Repair and amplify the tagmented DNA to produce the rightmost library fragments with P5/P7 and Index 2/Index 1. Retain the combined caption as one broad transformation; no additional cleanup or pooling is shown.
operations.mechanism: Gap repair and PCR are explicitly labelled; the output shows the completed adapter/index arrangement.
operations.information_effect: The DNA insert represents nuclear RNA sequence; the indices provide library indexing at the depicted interface. In single-nucleus libraries, gene-assigned reads can report relative transcript representation, and sequence reads can support splice-variant and mutation observations as described in the Grindberg abstract. The figure does not establish UMI-based absolute counting, complete RNA recovery, or whole-cell transcript equivalence.

method_scopes.rationale: All seven operations are local instances in the middle snRNA-Seq row. The initial Single cell and polyA RNA icons annotate the cellular source and analyte, rather than an RNA-extraction route preceding cell suspension. The nuclei fraction proceeds to sorting while supernatant has no drawn continuation. The listed Grindberg 2013 citation and its abstract resolve the single-nucleus RNA-to-cDNA target at schematic level; they do not verify every drawn end group or enzyme. Smart-Seq2/FRISCR rows and the LNA legend are separate context. The Lacar 2016 full text describes a later snRNA-seq implementation with additional staining/platform choices and is assessed as background without transferring those steps into this row.

unknowns.question: Which reverse transcriptase, CCC-generating reaction, G-rich end-handle composition and second-strand completion implement the drawn first-strand-to-cDNA/PCR transition in the Grindberg-associated row? The snRNA-Seq row does not label them and the supplied Grindberg evidence is abstract-only; primary protocol text would be needed for a mechanistic assignment. How is RNA made accessible from the sorted individual nucleus before first-strand synthesis? The arrow compresses that interface; a protocol passage would be needed to add a distinct nuclear-disruption or RNA-isolation operation. No such operation is asserted here.
